rows: You're good once you get someone on the mat. I won't be giving you that starting position for free.
You can put a dent in somebody. The question is whether you know what to do next.
When you're in the air you've got one way down. That's when I expect to meet you.
You can stretch the evening out all you want. I'm not standing about on your timetable.
They've all made the effort to get here. Both of us have a responsibility to make it worth it.
I'll keep it brief. You've got a match coming that deserves your attention.
They can put me in whatever slot they like. When I come through the curtain, that's the main attraction.
Look at me a moment. That's what you've got to deal with.
You can refuse the invitation. I'm not asking you to sit down of your own accord.
We'll talk about the value of a hard shot after you've taken one.
Knowing where I'm coming down is only useful if you're still there to meet me.
I'm taking the time I need. You're welcome to try to hurry me.
That's a decent sentiment. Can you deliver on it?
You're telling me you're the main event. That's something the room gets to decide.
You've named your {strength}. Fine. That's what I've prepared to deal with.
{strength}: that is your answer. Now we're getting somewhere.
I've no personal quarrel with you. I have a professional interest in the result.
We don't need a scene. Meet me at the bell.
I know what happens when people start shouting. I'd sooner have a match.
One fall, no guests. Are we clear?
All right, we'll meet on the mat. You can show me how good you are.
Stay on the canvas and see how you get on.
Don't disappear through the ropes when the conversation gets difficult.
Then we both know where we stand.
Come back to what I asked you. Not the question you'd prefer.
That will do, then. I'll give you that one.
Good. That's a useful place to leave it.
I'm expecting a hard night's work. I'm going to win it.
Let me be clear. I'm winning this match.
One clean pin, mid-match. Nobody needs to check the small print.
I've made my point. See you in there.
I've got my own approach to this. You'll see it at the bell.
You want something I can actually demonstrate. I haven't got that for this accusation, so I'm not using it.
That isn't a point I can back up. I'd rather put a proper problem in front of you when we wrestle.
Fine. The accusation goes. The challenge stays.
Right, that's one thing settled. Now let's find out what you've got in the ring.
Whether you can solve the problem I put in front of you. They'll see every move we make.
They'll see if you can get out of the positions I put you in. That's something we can actually test.
All right, leave that out of it. What can you actually show these people when the bell goes?
We've both got a match to wrestle. What do you reckon we can settle in there?
You've budgeted for my {strength}. Don't expect me to stick to your timetable when you try to contain them.
You've announced how you'll deal with my {strength}. That gives the room something to watch for when we get in there.
All right. I won't ask you to take my word for something neither of us can establish.
Fair correction. Let's give the people a contest they can judge with their own eyes.
You know the usual ways into a hold. I'm not giving you the usual starting position.
All that experience still needs an opening. I intend to make you earn it.
Experience means spotting the second threat before I've committed to stopping the first.
I've learned to keep a useful position even when the move I wanted isn't there.
You've prepared for the hold. What have you prepared for when I deny you the grip?
Studying the finish is easy. Tell me how you plan to get through the positions before it.
I study the transitions, not just the holds. The opportunity usually comes between the two.
My preparation starts with the first grip and branches from there. I don't need the exchange to follow a script.
